payload.title: Progression and evidence

sections.heading: Sequence
sections.text: Diagnose whole-number place value; reteach using a chart if needed. Model decimal places, guide responses, then require independent production. Compare decimals using equal units, teach against digit-count errors, then withhold assistance during end checks.

sections.heading: Delayed and new contexts
sections.text: Propose a delayed check after at least seven days, subject to an approved grade/subject policy. Use an unfamiliar measurement table for transfer. Neither opportunity is learning evidence until independently completed and verified.

payload.title: Place chart and practice sheet

sections.heading: Prerequisite fallback
sections.text: Draw columns labelled tens and ones. Put 4 in tens and 2 in ones. Explain how 42 differs from 24. If unsure, make four groups of ten marks and two single marks. Repeat with 31, then remove the drawing.

sections.heading: Faded decimal support
sections.text: Add tenths and hundredths columns. Place 3.25 in the chart. State each digit's value. Cover the labels and explain 7.46. Finally work without the chart: compare 0.2 and 0.19 using equal place units.

payload.textAlternative:

payload.title: Teacher guide

sections.heading: Before instruction
sections.text: Administer the quiz as a diagnostic without feedback. Route tens/ones errors to the worksheet. Keep this separate from the end-of-unit measure. All numerical contexts in this package are invented classroom examples, not reported local measurements or prices.

sections.heading: Differentiation and independence
sections.text: Offer oral directions, large print and a place chart during instruction. Fade the chart before the independent stage. A scribe may transcribe without supplying steps. Record tutoring, hints and collaboration as assistance. Do not count assisted work as independent evidence.

sections.heading: Assessment and follow-up
sections.text: Use the withheld summative form after instruction. Score reasoning through authorized human moderation using the protected rubric. Plan delayed retrieval only after policy approval. Revisit the misconception scene when learners compare by digit count.

payload.title: Text alternatives

sections.heading: Place chart in reading order
sections.text: Column one: tens. Column two: ones. Column three: tenths. Column four: hundredths. Read each digit with its column label. A blank place represents zero units of that size.

sections.heading: Practical alternative
sections.text: Instead of drawing shaded strips, make two text rows. Row one: four tenths equals forty hundredths. Row two: thirty-five hundredths. Compare their quantities verbally, then write your reason. The response can be typed, dictated or handwritten.

sections.heading: Non-gating extension
sections.text: Imagine a counting system in which each place to the left is worth five times its neighbour. Invent notation for six objects and eleven objects, and explain your rules.
